subsystems.name: Robot body and effector
subsystems.role: performs the therapeutic action at cellular scale.

subsystems.name: Propulsion and steering
subsystems.role: moves robots through tissue and blood using external fields or chemical gradients.

subsystems.name: Swarm control and localisation
subsystems.role: coordinates many units and tracks them inside the body.

subsystems.name: Payload and targeting
subsystems.role: releases drugs or acts only on diseased cells.

subsystems.name: Power and communication
subsystems.role: supplies energy without onboard batteries; no wires at this scale.

subsystems.name: Safety and clearance
subsystems.role: ensures robots degrade or leave the body after the procedure.

buildSteps.title: Design the robot and swarm behaviour
buildSteps.detail: Choose size (nanometres to microns), material and task; define how units cooperate and how they will be removed.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate bodies
buildSteps.detail: Top-down lithography for micro-scale units, or bottom-up self-assembly (DNA origami, block copolymers, magnetic nanoparticle clusters) for nanoscale units.

buildSteps.title: Functionalise surfaces
buildSteps.detail: Attach drugs, targeting molecules and antifouling coatings; load payloads.

buildSteps.title: Add propulsion
buildSteps.detail: Embed magnetic material or shape the body asymmetrically so external fields or chemical gradients drive motion.

buildSteps.title: Test in microfluidic models
buildSteps.detail: Measure speed, steering, drug release and cell-level effects in channels that mimic blood vessels.

buildSteps.title: Test in animals
buildSteps.detail: Use small animals to study navigation, imaging, immune response and clearance.

buildSteps.title: Build closed-loop control
buildSteps.detail: Combine real-time imaging with external field generators to steer swarms to a target and stop them.

buildSteps.title: Prepare for clinical use
buildSteps.detail: Develop sterile manufacturing, dosing, safety and regulatory pathways; none exists for autonomous surgical nanobots.

prerequisites.why: DNA origami and nanoparticle assembly work in the lab, but not at millions of identical surgical units.
Existing MRI and ultrasound cannot track individual nanobots in real time inside the body.
Magnetic and acoustic propulsion have been demonstrated in vitro and in small animals, but efficiency and depth are limited.
Simple swarms of magnetic particles have been steered in the lab, but not with cell-level precision.
Some nanomaterials clear from the body, but ensuring no toxic residue after surgery is unsolved.

pathway.milestone: Individual magnetic microrobots and acoustic particle swarms demonstrated in lab and small animals for targeted drug delivery
pathway.unlocks: basic propulsion, imaging and biocompatibility data.

pathway.milestone: Closed-loop systems that guide simple particle swarms to a tumour or clot in humans
Biodegradable nanobots that perform local drug release or mechanical action and then clear safely
Coordinated nanoscale swarms capable of cellular-level cutting, repair or ablation
pathway.unlocks: internal surgery without incisions, if imaging, power and control are solved.
